en: Itivuttaka 103: Catukkanipāta, Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus it was said. In this connection, monks, it has been said: "One who possesses four qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is a speaker of Dhamma, one who speaks at the proper time, speaks what is true, speaks what is beneficial, speaks on the Dhamma and the Discipline, and whose speech is timely, factual, meaningful, connected with the Dhamma, and connected with the Discipline.

One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is a giver of Dhamma, one who gives at the proper time, gives what is true, gives what is beneficial, gives the Dhamma and the Discipline, and whose giving is timely, factual, meaningful, connected with the Dhamma, and connected with the Discipline. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is a sacrificer of Dhamma, one who sacrifices at the proper time, sacrifices what is true, sacrifices what is beneficial, sacrifices the Dhamma and the Discipline, and whose sacrifice is timely, factual, meaningful, connected with the Dhamma, and connected with the Discipline. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is a receiver of Dhamma, one who receives at the proper time, receives what is true, receives what is beneficial, receives the Dhamma and the Discipline, and whose receiving is timely, factual, meaningful, connected with the Dhamma, and connected with the Discipline. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is one who has entered the stream, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms, firmly established, destined for full enlightenment. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained the true goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through final knowledge. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is one who has entered upon the way, one who has entered the path, one who has set out toward the goal. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is one who has abandoned the five lower fetters. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four? Here, monks, a brahmin is one who is well-born on both sides, of pure descent for seven generations, unblemished, not suspected of being born from an illicit union; he is learned, possessing a vast knowledge of the mantras and having mastered the sciences; he is virtuous, endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, possessed of restraint and guarded in his conduct; and he is one who has abandoned the five higher fetters. One who possesses these four qualities, monks, is a brahmin. And it has also been said: "One who possesses four other qualities is a brahmin. And what, monks, are those four?

The Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand as it really is: ‘This is suffering’;”
“Those who do not understand as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering’;
who do not understand as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; who do not understand as it really is:
‘This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering’—these, monks, whether they be ascetics or brahmins, are not reckoned among the ascetics or the brahmins.”

They are esteemed as brahmins, yet these venerable ones do not themselves, by means of direct knowledge, realize and dwell having attained the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminship in this very life.
But those, monks, who are ascetics or brahmins that understand “this is suffering” as it truly is;
‘This is the origin of suffering,’ they understand as it really is; ‘This is the cessation of suffering,’ they understand as it really is;
‘This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering,’ they understand as it really is.
These, monks, among ascetics and brahmins, are truly ascetics and truly brahmins.

And they are esteemed as brahmins; moreover, those venerable ones, having realized for themselves through direct higher knowledge in this very life the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood, dwell having attained them.
Thus the Blessed One spoke on this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
"Those who do not understand suffering,
nor the origin of suffering;"
And where suffering ceases entirely without remainder,
they do not know that path.
They lead to the subsiding of suffering.
Yet they are deficient in the liberation of mind,
as well as in the liberation by wisdom.
They are incapable of making an end;
they indeed go on to birth and old age.
But those who understand suffering—
Furthermore, the origin of suffering,
and where suffering ceases without remainder in its entirety.
And they understand that path leading to the subsiding of suffering,
being perfected in the liberation of mind.
And likewise for liberation through wisdom;
they are capable of making an end,
they do not undergo birth and old age.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth [sutta].
